class: A second, weaker copy of a decision: the job's title and employer read from page chrome by a reader that ignored the shared helpers
symptom: Forterra on Rippling (ats.rippling.com/forterra/jobs/...), 30 September: the job was recorded as 'Unknown Role @ Ats' and the tailored resume attached to the application was named ..._Resume_Ats.pdf, although the page's title is 'Senior Staff Network Systems Engineer' and its share title says '| Forterra Careers'.
site: Rippling; any posting read by the plain page reader (no JSON-LD, no platform API)
root_cause: fetch_generic_job looked for a bare '<title>' (Rippling writes <title data-rh="true">) and named the company after the host's first label ('ats'), with its own prefix list, instead of the helpers the rendered reader already used (_clean_page_title, _employer_named_in, _company_from_url). _company_from_url's hand-kept vendor list lacked Rippling and its prefix list lacked 'ats.'.
why_tests_missed: The generic reader was only met with pages whose <title> had no attributes and whose host named the employer.
fix: page_identity(html, text, url) is the one reading of a page's title and employer: og:title or <title> with any attributes, cleaned of the site name; the employer from the site's own name (og:site_name or the part after ' | ', never a vendor's name), then the equal-opportunity sentence, then the address. ATS_VENDORS is one list of hosting vendors (Rippling, Workable, Jobvite, UKG and others added), and 'ats.', 'boards.' and 'hire.' are generic host labels.
prevention: One function names a job from a page, and every reader calls it; a vendor that hosts many employers is data in one list, and its name is never taken for the employer.
